entities.name: BRAF
observations: BRAF V600E is useful as a reflex tumor test after dMMR/MSI testing in colorectal cancer when MLH1/PMS2 expression is lost.
BRAF V600E positivity strongly supports sporadic MLH1-silenced colorectal cancer but does not independently diagnose or absolutely exclude Lynch syndrome.

entities.name: Lynch syndrome
observations: BRAF V600E-negative status does not establish Lynch syndrome because sporadic MLH1-deficient tumors may be BRAF wild type.
Strong family history or clinical suspicion warrants germline evaluation even when tumor triage suggests a sporadic mechanism.

entities.name: Colorectal cancer
observations: BRAF V600E is most relevant in colorectal tumors with MLH1/PMS2 loss after MMR immunohistochemistry or MSI testing.

Reported BRAF V600E frequency among MLH1-methylated sporadic tumors is approximately 69–78% in published summaries, with substantial population variation; one Chinese cohort reported 15/155 MLH1-loss tumors (9.7%).

entities.name: Bethesda BRAF triage
observations: Revised Bethesda criteria are a preselection tool and can miss germline MMR mutation carriers; BRAF testing should be embedded in a sequential MMR/MSI-to-germline algorithm rather than used alone.
BRAF has little role in isolated MSH2, MSH6, or PMS2 loss without MLH1 loss.
